newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel steady on strong demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel steady on strong demand.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel prices were steady Friday on continued agricultural demand in the Midwest that was supporting basis on October barrels.
Buying interest was expected to continue into next week as the autumn harvest shifted into high gear in the region, boosting demand for low sulphur diesel fuel.
"You should see a lot of pulls from terminals," one trader said.
Unleaded gasoline basis also was drawing support from talk of refinery outages and turnarounds that fueled refiner buying this week, traders said.
Texaco was set to begin a turnaround at its 94,600 barrel per day El Dorado, Kansas refinery over the weekend.

Farmland Industries Inc was expected to return to service by midweek a catalytic cracker at its 75,000 barrel per day Coffeyville, Kansas refinery. The two-week outage had cut crude runs in half but was no longer a market factor.
The Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of petroleum inventories in the region, had a 29-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 20-day supply of unleaded gasoline on hand.
Chicago prompt October unleaded gasoline differentials were talked even to 0.25 cent a gallon over the print, with later deliveries 1.25/1.0 cent under and premium 3.0 cents higher.
Group Three unleaded eased to 0.75/0.50 cent a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and was heard done 1.15 cent under for later deliveries, with premium remaining 2.50 cents higher.
